messages:
incident-bot: :warning: PROD anomaly detected: spike in 5xx responses from svc-auth and svc-a after deploy. Paging maya (on-call).

pagerduty-bot: Triggered PD incident INC-2026-0315 -> maya (primary) and sam (backup).

maya: I'm awake, looking. What changed in the deploy?

jon: We deployed canary group for release v2026.03.15 about 12m ago. CI ran `kms-rotate` job as part of release tasks. Canary started returning 502/503s ~5m after deploy.

sam: logs?

jon: excerpt from svc-auth log: 
```
2026-03-15T02:14:08Z ERROR secret_fetcher: failed to decrypt: AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:acct:key/0a1b2c3d 
stack=runtime/secret_fetcher.go:78
```

linda: That looks like the new key doesn't have a grant for the EC2/EKS node role. We rotated the key but didn't add the decryption principal to the key policy or create a grant.

maya: What's the blast radius? How many requests failing?

eric: Cloud metrics: canary pods serving ~18% of traffic, error rate for canary group peaked at 22% across endpoints. Global error bump ~3.5%. Roughly 5 enterprise customers saw at least one timeout. Support already got 2 tickets.

sam: Options: (A) flip feature flag so traffic doesn't hit the new code path, (B) create an emergency grant on the key to allow decrypt for the runtime role, (C) rollback canary.

maya: We should minimize customer impact quickly. Fastest is flag kill-switch if feature flag exists. If not, rollback. Which feature flags are in play?

jon: We have `feature.embed_new_path` ON for canary. It routes secret access through the rotated key. I can toggle it for canary and prod.

jon: toggling now:
```
ldctl environment toggle feature.embed_new_path canary false --reason "prod KMS rotate causing decrypt failures"
```
jon: :white_check_mark: flag off for canary. Monitoring.

ops-bot: Canary traffic now routed to baseline variant.

maya: error rate drop?

eric: error rate for canary down to 2.1% within 90s. Global back to 0.6% above baseline. Still a tail from background jobs hitting secret store.

linda: Background workers use a different role (worker-role) that may still be using rotated key. We should either add a grant or schedule a rollback of key rotation.

sam: Can we do an emergency grant on the new key that authorizes decrypt for both `redwood-prod-node-role` and `redwood-prod-worker-role`? That would re-enable canary code without rolling back code.

maya: It's riskier but lower blast than full rollback. What's the command?

linda: Example AWS CLI create-grant (one-time grant; needs KMS:CreateGrant permission):
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:acct:key/0a1b2c3d \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::acct:role/redwood-prod-node-role \
  --operations Decrypt Encrypt --name emergency-grant-20260315
```
We need to create a second grant for worker-role.

jon: I can run that but need approval - emergency change. maya, you ok?

maya: Approve for immediate mitigation. Make sure to log the grant IDs and plan to revoke after we implement proper key policy.

jon: running grants now...
jon: :white_check_mark: grants created. IDs: g-abc123, g-def456.

incident-bot: Detected grant creation on KMS key by jon.

eric: background job errors subsided within 2 minutes. Error rate baseline restored.

maya: Good. Now we need a safe durable fix: either (1) apply permanent key policy update that allows the runtime roles to decrypt, (2) or revert key rotation and map alias back to previous key, or (3) rework deploy so rotation occurs only after policy updates.

sam: I'll open an emergency PR to infra with key policy change and include tests in staging. We should avoid alias swap in prod unless necessary.

linda: Agree. Key policy change is the right direction. We'll keep the grants in place temporarily. Also add preflight check in CI that validates the KMS key policy includes decrypt for required principals before rotation step completes.

maya: Customer comms?

eric: Support will update the 3 impacted customers with root cause and mitigation. Estimated RTO for permanent fix: 2 hours to get PR reviewed and staged, longer for scheduled maintenance to rotate keys properly.

maya: On-call handoff: eric, you're primary for monitoring for next 45m. Pager duty threshold: if global error rate >1.5% for 5m, page me.

eric: ack. I'll watch pod logs and metrics.

incident-bot: Incident severity set to SEV2 by maya. Action items assigned.

jon: I've documented exact deploy steps and CI job names in PR #812. Also adding a preflight validator script to verify KMS grants/key policy before `rotate-kms` job runs.

sam: PR #813 created: infra/iam/kms-key-policy patch adding statements for both node and worker roles. Marked emergency; includes staging smoke test plan.

linda: We should also add a rollback signal to the deploy pipeline: if any canary shows secret decrypt errors (logs match KMS AccessDenied), abort rollout and flip feature flag automatically. I'll draft the pipeline rule.

maya: Good. Post-incident checklist: (a) permanent key policy PR + staging test, (b) CI preflight validator, (c) pipeline abort rule for secret-decrypt errors, (d) update runbook and run a drill for KMS rotation, (e) customer followups.

jon: Putting timeline in incident tracker: 
- 02:10 deploy started (canary)
- 02:15 KMS rotation job ran
- 02:18 first 5xx observed
- 02:22 pager duty page fired
- 02:24 feature flag kill-switch applied for canary
- 02:27 emergency KMS grants created
- 02:30 errors subsided to baseline

maya: Great. I'll own the postmortem write-up and RCA. Will include sequence, root cause (rotation without policy/grants), mitigation, and follow-ups.

eric: handing monitoring back to maya in 30m if stable.

linda: Thanks team. Leaving notes for infra on-call to watch KMS key state.

maya: Closing live page; keeping thread open for postmortem links and PR reviews. Thanks everyone. :white_heart:
